This document outlines the major maintenance procedures P1, which must be performed 
every years as indicated by Y in the title block

The first draft initiated by eng. at Alwahat Albahria substation, accepted by eng. : general director, approved 
by eng. 
Head sector, and certified by eng. 
Ahmed Saied Abdelazez: ME zone EETC quality control general director, MPIS Coordinator.

items:
A work permit must be issued and the qualified maintenance staff should carry the 
 suitable safety category
Safety fence with caution marks surrounding the work area is required
Wear your safety and healthy equipment as safety helmet, safety shoes, ... etc
The work must be done in a cleaned area or in workshop.

The circuit breaker must be isolated and properly earthed at both sides, it 
 should be in ON position.
Disconnect DC Voltage.

Close and open the breaker to make sure that the opening and closing spring 
 are released before starting the work.

Don't throw any oil into the sewage 
 because the oil prevents the sewage treatment process.

Collect the oil that drained out of the 
 poles into a barrel and return it back to the vendor to recycle it to save 
 money.

Collect the oil used in washing the 
 poles in another barrel and do not re-use it for filling the poles unless 
 filtered, dried and its dielectric strength measured with an oil tester (not 
 less than 40kv/2.5 mm).

Don't burn cloth used in cleaning but 
 collect it and send it to the dump
One set of metric open end box wrenches size 13mm to 24mm.

Adjustable spanner, one set of screw drivers, torque wrench, fine file, fine 
 emery cloth, and wipers.
Complete set of gaskets for the circuit breaker.
One barrel of new oil (its dielectric strength not less than 40kv/2.5)
Dielectric strength oil tester.
Some of gasoline, lubricating oil, grease.
Clean pails for changing oil.
Tin cans to hold bolts, nuts, studs, washers, ... etc.

sections.text:
Inspection of Fixed 
Contact & Moving Contact

items:
Make sure that the 
 breaker is open.

Drain the oil out by 
 removing the oil drain plug and allow the oil to drain out of pole into a 
 container placed under each pole.

Unscrew the metal cap 
 to the insulating cylinder and raise it up with the upper connection.

Lift the fixed 
 contact, unscrew the screw of the insulating cover of the fixed contact

Take off the 
 insulating cylinder.

Inspect the fixed 
 contact elements and the contact springs.

If the contact 
 elements and the contact springs are in good condition and not deteriorated, 
 clean them with new oil and clean cloth, then reassemble the fixed contact as 
 follows:

Place the insulating 
 cylinder to the porter of contact.

Fit the screw to fix 
 insulating cylinder.

Place the fixed 
 contact into the pole in its previous place.

Remove the 4 screws 
 that fixing the insulating cylinder to the lower terminal part and unscrew the 
 screw fixing the insulating cylinder to the circuit breaker back cover.

Remove the 4 screws 
 fixing the insulating cylinder to the oil pump.

Lift the insulating 
 cylinder and lay it gently on a clean board, take care not to damage the lower 
 face.

Unscrew the screw that 
 fixing the arc chamber to the Aluminum cylinder base and pull out the arc 
 chamber.

If the arc chambers 
 are not deteriorated, clean them with new oil and clean wipers, change it, 
 pull out the sliding contact, then locate the new one with the sliding contact 
 in the insulating cylinder.

Unscrew the two screws 
 that fixing the Aluminum cylinder to the lower terminal and pull out the 
 Aluminum cylinder.

Pull out the lower 
 terminal with the sliding blades for the inspection of the moving contact rod.

If the tip of the 
 contact rod is badly deteriorated it must be replaced.

Before starting 
 drainage the oil out of the poles be sure that the breaker is in open 
 position, then remove the outlet plug and allow all oil to drain out of poles 
 into container replaced under each pole.

Close the outlet 
 plugs, open the filling plugs at the top of each pole and pour oil into each 
 pole.

After oil has reached 
 the oil level indicators close and trip the breaker three times to wash the 
 arc chambers, and contact.

Remove the outlet 
 plugs and allow all oil to drain out of the poles.

Repeat the previous 
 steps until you find the drainage oil to be cleaned.

Refill the poles with 
 oil of dielectric strength not less than 30kv/mm, during filling the breaker 
 must be in open position and oil must be poured into each pole till the right 
 mark on the oil level indicators.

Wait a few minutes and 
 if the oil level has lowered, fill up to the right mark.

Before putting the 
 circuit breaker into service, it is necessary to carryout some hand closing 
 and opening operations to make sure that the operating mechanism works 
 satisfactorily and carryout some electrical closing and opening operations to 
 make sure that connection are right and that the closing operating mechanism 
 operates satisfactorily.

For hand closing 
 operation, insert the detachable crank into its place and manually rotate the 
 main shaft in clockwise until the free rotation of the shaft, the state of 
 springs is indicated by a colored indicator on the cover of the operating 
 mechanism (Red spring loaded, white spring released), then turn in clockwise 
 to direction of the mark "1". The state of the breaker is indicated by a 
 colored indicator on the cover of the operating mechanism (Red spring closed, 
 white spring released ).

To trip the breaker 
 turn the crank in anti clockwise to the direction of the mark "O".

Check that the 
 releases trip the breaker satisfactorily.

Check that the 
 auxiliary switch works satisfactorily.

If closing springs are 
 released, the motor when energized loads the springs and stops automatically 
 as soon as springs are fully loaded.

If the breaker works 
 with the series releases, adjust the trip setting of releases.

Clean the mechanism 
 parts by means of a paint brush drenched with diesel oil and petrol, be sure 
 that the breaker is open and springs are released before starting cleaning.

Clean the metal parts 
 by means of a clean dry duster and clean the insulating parts by means of 
 another dry duster.

After making sure that 
 the operating mechanism is in good working condition and that the pole are 
 filled with oil at the right level, the breaker can be put into service.

Finally record all 
 that has been done on the maintenance card of the circuit breaker.
